annotation.authors_or_issuer: Weßel, M.; Ellerich-Groppe, N.; Koppelin, F.; Schweda, M.
key_provisions_or_claims: Gender and age stereotyping in eldercare robots is proposed to boost acceptance but raises autonomy and discrimination concerns.
16 interviews with developers, industry and nursing stakeholders.
Six approaches identified: negation, functionalistic relativization, explanation, neutralization, stereotyping, queering.
Ethical implications discussed through professional responsibility.
Calls for responsible age tech in pluralistic societies.
annotation.summary_en: Qualitative interview study (16 stakeholders from technology development, industry and nursing) on how gender and age stereotypes in eldercare robots are perceived. It identifies six approaches to stereotypes and discusses ethical implications for professional responsibility and responsible age tech.
annotation.title_clean: Gender and Age Stereotypes in Robotics for Eldercare: Ethical Implications of Stakeholder Perspectives from Technology Development, Industry, and Nursing
annotation.title_en: Gender and Age Stereotypes in Robotics for Eldercare: Ethical Implications of Stakeholder Perspectives from Technology Development, Industry, and Nursing
